title: Sample unary fragmentation families and repair the large-volume comparison
statement: The original19F1 comparison retaining only Ai->Aj is FALSE in general: A<->2B, unit rates,c=(1,1),w=(2,1),x0=(1,0),n=1,T=1 gives full P(0,2)=[1-exp(-(1+2/V))]/(1+2/V)->1-e^-1 while the claimed reference stays put. Root repair retains ALL source-arity1 channels Ai->z including fragmentation and diffusion. Each ancestral family conserves its one-molecule mass and has <=C=ceil(wmax/wmin) particles. Enumerate its actual finite graph, at most binom(nd+C,C) configurations; family rates have polynomial binary height. Distinct initial families are independent because no reaction has multiple parents; projection of summed family propensities is exactly the population generator, even when collocated. Fast-forward each of nd family types with the paid finite-generator operation. For binary x0_a, draw its polynomial-category endpoint histogram using sequential fixed U<->V DDB1 binomials, then aggregate count times configuration. No numeric-N0 loop. Row-TV epsilon/[8max(1,N0)] and total binomial error<=epsilon/8 give unconditional TV control, every-run polynomial complete-binary resources and valid original-class output. This source-unary reference need not be complex balanced or weakly reversible. Its mass bound gives population<=C*N0. Every omitted reaction now has source arity a>=2 and total rate<=kappa(C*N0)^a/V. With A=max(2,max a), K=sum_omitted kappa*max(1,C)^a, first-omitted-event coupling gives TV(X(T),Y(T))<=min(1,K*T*(1+N0)^A/V). Use this sampler only when that paid bound meets the error budget. This does not resolve general interaction loads.
